subject: Whoa J&As — Oct 15: HUD sole-sources $170M property-preservation contracts after vendors suspended operations over unpaid invoices
body:
## 1. HUD sole-sources $170M property-preservation contracts after vendors suspended operations over unpaid invoices

**HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT, DEPARTMENT OF · Alpine Companies Inc. · $170,829,743 (total incl. options) · 41 USC 3304 (a)(2); FAR Overhaul 6.103-2**  
*Posted 2026-10-14, award {3A_4A}_Contract_86614526D00001_{5A_8A}_Contract_86614526D00002_{3S_5S}_Contract_86614526D00007_{4S_6S}_Contract_86614526D00008, “Field Service Management Services 3.12 Areas [3A/4A]_ [5A/8A]_1D_2D [4D/5D] [3S/5S] [4S/6S]”*

HUD cites unusual and compelling urgency for follow-on Field Service Management contracts in eight areas. It says it chose not to exercise the next option because of poor performance: key vendors suspended operations over outstanding invoices, and non-payments escalated to Congressional inquiries.

> “key vendors suspending operations because of outstanding client invoices, lack of property preservation and maintenance triggering property liens and blocking the marketing or sale of homes, and non-payments escalated to Congressional inquiries”  
> — JOFOC Number 26-30_FSM_COMP-ADVOC_SIGNED.pdf, p. 3

[SAM.gov notice](https://sam.gov/opp/9ca2e17f9368437baa365b7db8ee0c23/view) · [JOFOC Number 26-30_FSM_COMP-ADVOC_SIGNED.pdf](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abigailhaddad/federal-ja-documents/resolve/e93882dcc18c1d76244974093b3696fd5e5e016e/files/9ca2e17f9368437baa365b7db8ee0c23/26c620cab19e4407b47991701fc1fd1f_JOFOC_Number_26-30_FSM_COMP-ADVOC_SIGNED.pdf) · [Signed Cancelled solicitation 86614526R00001 (19).pdf](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abigailhaddad/federal-ja-documents/resolve/e93882dcc18c1d76244974093b3696fd5e5e016e/files/9ca2e17f9368437baa365b7db8ee0c23/ee464b2e7c4247e29dc1e3b6231d7bac_Signed_Cancelled_solicitation_86614526R00001_19_.pdf)

## 2. DTRA reprocures nuclear-enterprise cyber toolkits after terminating first contractor for cause

**DEFENSE THREAT REDUCTION AGENCY (DTRA) (DEPT OF DEFENSE) · NextCom LLC · $5,000,000 (ceiling) · 41 U.S.C. 1901**  
*Posted 2026-10-14, award HDTRA126PE017, “Advanced Cyber Security Threat Detection Analysis Platform”*

DTRA proposes a new sole-source award to NextCom LLC after the prior contractor failed to deliver conforming products and was terminated for cause. It says reopening competition would take an estimated six to nine months, and initial units are needed within 30 days.

> “The contractor subsequently failed to deliver conforming products, and the Government terminated the contract for cause.”  
> — MobileKit_Reprocurement_JA_Final_20260916_Redacted.pdf, p. 2

[SAM.gov notice](https://sam.gov/opp/e0ef04062f9c4b32833b5e196f831b1c/view) · [MobileKit_Reprocurement_JA_Final_20260916_Redacted.pdf](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abigailhaddad/federal-ja-documents/resolve/e93882dcc18c1d76244974093b3696fd5e5e016e/files/e0ef04062f9c4b32833b5e196f831b1c/07467b57740745138f8314db5ac8af51_MobileKit_Reprocurement_JA_Final_20260916_Redacted.pdf)

## 3. State extends Deloitte AI and sanctions support up to two years, no ceiling

**STATE, DEPARTMENT OF · Deloitte Consulting LLP · value redacted · GSAR 538.7104-3, paragraph (b)(iii)**  
*Posted 2026-10-14, award 19AQMM19A0280, “GSAR 538.7104-3 Sole source justification”*

State proposes a one-year extension plus two six-month options for Deloitte's call covering AI development and sanctions work. The document says the BPA and call had no maximum ceiling and that, given the recent reorganization and staffing levels, changing contractors would be highly disruptive.

> “Given the recent Department reorganization and current staffing levels, a change in contract at this point would be highly disruptive to TFS core efforts.”  
> — LSJ Template CfA PMSS Deloitte_Redacted.pdf, p. 2

[SAM.gov notice](https://sam.gov/opp/748a34bba7e4494faae508cb0bb33b3f/view) · [LSJ Template CfA PMSS Deloitte_Redacted.pdf](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abigailhaddad/federal-ja-documents/resolve/e93882dcc18c1d76244974093b3696fd5e5e016e/files/748a34bba7e4494faae508cb0bb33b3f/9b8abe6139ba44e3980098ca643dffbc_LSJ_Template_CfA_PMSS_Deloitte_Redacted.pdf)

## 4. DCMA plans $90M ServiceNow expansion, including fraud detection and FMS budget tracking

**DEFENSE CONTRACT MANAGEMENT AGENCY (DCMA) (DEPT OF DEFENSE) · Carahsoft Technology Corp. · $90,467,668 (total incl. options) · 41 U.S.C. 152(3 as prescribed in FAR 8.401 and 538.7104-3(b)(ii)**  
*Posted 2026-10-14, award N6600119A0120, “Platform Automation, Implementation, Sustainment, Operations and Licensing”*

DCMA proposes a one-year base plus four option years with Carahsoft to sustain and expand its ServiceNow platform with seventeen new capabilities. The document says the services are integrally related to the proprietary platform and DCMA's configuration.

> “Overall Total Contract Amount: $90,467,667.83”  
> — TAB A -JA_CAFM_ServiceNowExpansion-v2_redacted1_Redacted.pdf, p. 1 (machine-transcribed page)

[SAM.gov notice](https://sam.gov/opp/7716091b214f4c8a9aedd224690fcdba/view) · [TAB A -JA_CAFM_ServiceNowExpansion-v2_redacted1_Redacted.pdf](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abigailhaddad/federal-ja-documents/resolve/e93882dcc18c1d76244974093b3696fd5e5e016e/files/7716091b214f4c8a9aedd224690fcdba/dd9805aa900a45179476c3ecd8936386_TAB_A_-JA_CAFM_ServiceNowExpansion-v2_redacted1_Redacted.pdf)

## 5. VA sole-sources lab analyzers for a year after missing procurement package deadline, citing staffing shortages

**VETERANS AFFAIRS, DEPARTMENT OF · Beckman Coulter, Inc. · value redacted · GSAM/R 538.7104-3(b)(1)(ii)**  
*Posted 2026-10-14, award V797D70260, “6632--Chemistry Immunoassay CPRR”*

The VA is bridging East Orange VAMC's chemistry testing with Beckman Coulter for a year. The document attributes the prior sole source to extensive delays in submitting a long-term procurement package due to staffing shortages, and says the medical center missed its submission date.

> “because of the extensive delays in submitting a long-term procurement package due to staffing shortages.”  
> — FAR 8 Sole Source Justification - Redacted.pdf, p. 2

[SAM.gov notice](https://sam.gov/opp/0066d6a2728b45119df568aa08155572/view) · [FAR 8 Sole Source Justification - Redacted.pdf](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abigailhaddad/federal-ja-documents/resolve/e93882dcc18c1d76244974093b3696fd5e5e016e/files/0066d6a2728b45119df568aa08155572/d44daf023fdb491ab2683de11028f954_FAR_8_Sole_Source_Justification_-_Redacted.pdf) · [V797D70260 36C24227N0116_2.docx](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abigailhaddad/federal-ja-documents/resolve/e93882dcc18c1d76244974093b3696fd5e5e016e/files/0066d6a2728b45119df568aa08155572/b70110ae073a454b837921fdddac80d1_V797D70260_36C24227N0116_2.docx)
